notes: Derived from the verb susamak (to get thirsty). To say 'I am thirsty', Turkish uses the past tense of the verb: Susadım (literally 'I have become thirsty'), whereas susamış is mainly used before a noun or mean 'looking thirsty'.

faults.quote: Sıcak havada yürüyünce çok susamış hissettim.
faults.why: 'susamış hissettim' is an unnatural English calque ('felt thirsty'); 'susamış' is mainly attributive.
Learners must know that 'I am thirsty' is expressed verbally as 'Susadım', not with 'susamış'.
